newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia April trade data seen in deficit -poll.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia April trade data seen in deficit -poll.

text.p: Malaysia was expected to report an average trade deficit of 273.6 million ringgit for the month of April, according to a Reuter poll of nine economists.
But their estimates ranged widely, from a surplus of 50 million ringgit to a deficit of one billion ringgit, the poll conducted this week found.
Foreign exchange and stock market dealers said there was speculation the April trade data would be in deficit of up to two billion ringgit.
The deficit forecast for April compared with a 1.75 billion ringgit surplus reported in March, and a shortfall of 253.9 million in April a year ago.
Malaysia recorded a negative trade balance of 618 million ringgit in 1996. The government has forecast that the deficit would shrink to 340 million ringgit this year.
Officials at the Statistics Department which releases the monthly data, could not be immediately contacted to comment on when the data would be released.
The economists said there were wide variations in the forecasts as they could not tell how many aircraft purchases would be included in the monthly data released by the Statistics Department.
The economists polled were from Arab-Malaysian Securities, Capitalcorp Securities, Credit Lyonnais, ING Barings, Merrill Lynch, MMS International, Natwest Markets, UBS Securities and Vickers Ballas.
